Diagnose the GLM-AED mass balance

Source: R/glm_mass_balance.R
diag_glm_mass_balance.Rd

Computes, for each variable (or each AED total), the change in the in-lake inventory and the net external transport, and the remainder between them:

Usage

diag_glm_mass_balance(
  mb = NULL,
  by = c("total", "var"),
  aed_totals = NULL,
  path_glm = NULL,
  units = c("mmol", "kg"),
  plot = FALSE,
  aeme = NULL,
  path = NULL
)

Arguments

mb

tibble from read_glm_mass_balance(), or a path to mass_balance.csv. If NULL, it is read from aeme.

by

"total" (default) to diagnose the aed totals, or "var" to diagnose each variable in the file.

aed_totals

list; the aed_totals block (TN_vars, TN_varscale, ...), as built by derive_aed_totals(). Ignored if path_glm is given.

path_glm

character; GLM-AED model directory (containing aed/) to derive aed_totals from. Takes precedence over aed_totals.

units

"mmol" (default, AED native) or "kg", which converts using the molar masses of N, P and C. TSS is left unchanged when converted.

plot

logical; also return a ggplot of cumulative net_internal.

aeme

Aeme object. Used to read mb when it is NULL, and to locate the glm_aed configuration for the totals when neither aed_totals nor path_glm is given.

path

character; root directory used with aeme.

Value

a list with daily (tibble: datetime, name, interval_days, inflow, outflow, lake, d_lake, net_external, net_internal, cum_net_internal), summary (tibble: one row per name, with the mean inventory, total external flux, total internal remainder and its percentage of the mean inventory) and, if plot = TRUE, plot.

Details

net_internal = d(Lake) - (Inf - Out)

where d(Lake) is the change in the Lake term since the previous row and Inf/Out are the inflow and outflow totals over that same interval. GLM writes Inf and Out as totals over the save interval (nsave * dt), so the interval length of each row is taken from the time stamps and per-day rates (*_rate, mmol per day) are returned alongside the interval totals; use the rates to compare runs with different nsave. If path_glm (or aeme) is given, the time stamps are checked against nsave * dt in the GLM nml. net_internal is the amount gained or lost inside the lake (reactions, sediment and atmospheric exchange, repair of negative states). For conservative quantities it should be close to zero. For reactive variables it is expected to be non-zero, but for the totals TN, TP and TOC it is the net sediment/atmosphere exchange and should be small relative to the inventory.
